simple.meaning: יָבָם (yâbâm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a brother-in-law.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Deuteronomy, beginning at Deuteronomy 25:5. Its contexts include family, family line, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָבָם (H2993).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יָבָם (yâbâm) / H2993 is traced through Deuteronomy 25:5, Deuteronomy 25:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: If brothers dwell together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.

timeline.evidenceText: If brothers dwell together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.

If the man doesn’t want to take his brother’s wife, then his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to raise up to his brother a name in Israel. He will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother to me.”

definitions.full: H2993. yabam [ יָבָם ] noun masculine husband's brother (Late Hebrew id. ; יַבְמָא ᵑ7 ; see Lag M ii. 78 ) — only suffix יְבֶמִי Deut 25:7 , יְבָמָהּ 25:5 , in law of levirate marriage (compare Gen 38:8 ; see also Dr Deut 25:5-10 ).
